The must-sees

7 places Wizzy will tap you for first, each with a story and something to look for.

  1. 01
    Fortress

    Alcazaba

    It was built in the 11th century and enlarged under the Nasrids. Roman columns and capitals were reused in its gates.

    Look for

    Notice how the gates turn sharply as you climb: bent entrances built to slow attackers down.

  2. 02
    Market

    Atarazanas Market

    It was built in the 19th century on the site of a Nasrid shipyard, whose gate was kept. A large stained-glass window shows scenes of the city.

    Look for

    On the Nasrid gate, look for shields carved with the dynasty’s motto: there is no victor but God.

  3. 03
    Shopping · 1891

    Calle Larios

    It opened in 1891, funded by the Larios family and named after the Marquis. It links the port with Plaza de la Constitución.

    Look for

    At the port end stands Mariano Benlliure’s bronze monument to the Marquis of Larios, on a tall stone pedestal.

  4. 04
    Fortress

    Gibralfaro Castle

    Yusuf I of Granada built the castle in the 14th century to protect the Alcazaba. In 1487 it held out for months against the army of the Catholic Monarchs.

    Look for

    Inside the walls, find the Airón well, cut deep into the rock to keep the garrison in water through a siege.

  5. 05
    Church

    Málaga Cathedral

    Work began in 1528 and stopped in the 18th century before the south tower was completed. Locals call the building La Manquita, the one-armed lady.

    Look for

    Inside, the carved cedar choir stalls include saints by the Baroque sculptor Pedro de Mena.

  6. 06
    Museum

    Picasso Museum Málaga

    It opened in 2003 with works donated by the artist’s family. Phoenician and Roman remains are visible in the basement.

    Look for

    Look up inside: several rooms keep the palace’s carved wooden coffered ceilings.

  7. 07
    Landmark

    Roman Theatre

    It was built in the time of Augustus. It lay buried until 1951, when it was found during work on a cultural centre that was later demolished.

    Look for

    Stand on Calle Alcazabilla: the Roman seats climb straight up toward the Moorish walls of the Alcazaba.
